component.name: LecCheck
component.summary: Track the lectures, practices and labs you attend
מעקב אחרי הרצאות, תרגולים ומעבדות שהשתתפת בהם

description.p: Mark every class you attend during the semester and see your progress at a glance. LecCheck works offline and syncs live between your phone and computer.

ul.li: Today, Week and course pages with every lecture, practice and lab
Attendance requirements and statistics for each course
Reminders before class, and a quick question after it
Jewish and Israeli holidays as days without classes
English and Hebrew

screenshot.caption: Today: the class going on now and what's next

ul.li: A calmer way to mark a session. One Attended button with a menu for the other statuses replaces the green and red buttons; the color only shows once it's marked.
Today is less crowded: the session in the big card isn't listed again in the schedule.
Stats starts with your courses: overall attendance, then each course with its requirements under it. On phones the charts fold under More details.
Settings on phones is a short list of categories, each on its own page.
Days off stand out on Week: the whole day is tinted with its name at the top, and a new icon replaces the umbrella. The date stays visible.
A saved recording is one tap away: "Recording link" opens it, and Edit changes it.
Reception hours: turn them on in Settings → Courses, add them to a course like a meeting, and they show on Week as an outline. They never count toward attendance.

Import a timetable with a chatbot: copy LecCheck's prompt, give it to your own chatbot with a screenshot or file of your schedule, and bring back what it writes. It's checked and previewed, and only adds a new semester.
Clearer Hebrew: statuses read as nouns, like נוכחות and היעדרות, and other awkward wording is fixed.

Typing on desktop no longer loses letters. A key that's also a shortcut (T, the digits in a session's notes, Home, the arrows) was taken by the shortcut even in a text field, so the letter never appeared.
LecCheck looks for updates every time it starts, not once a day.
The countdown on Today shows days from 24 hours on, like "2d 3h".
Delete cloud data asks you to type DELETE first.
A Today button on Week, in words, takes you back to this week. The icon was easy to miss.
Ctrl+Z on Week undoes your last change: a move, a quick add or a mark.
The mouse wheel changes the week: Shift+wheel, a sideways scroll, or the wheel over the day names. The plain wheel still scrolls the hours and Ctrl+wheel still zooms.
Choose the tab LecCheck opens on, for each device, in Settings.
A keyring that doesn't answer can't stop a sign-out halfway.
Linux releases are only the Flatpak now: the tarball and install.sh are gone. Installs from 2.0.0-beta.15 move from inside the app.

LecCheck for Linux is a Flatpak, from its own repository (signed with its own key): flatpak install --user emanuel4100.github.io/LecCheck2/leccheck.flatpakref, or open that file in GNOME Software or Discover. It runs on the freedesktop runtime (about 300 MB, shared with other Flatpak apps) and updates itself from then on. This is the last version for install.sh.

Move to the Flatpak: LecCheck installed with install.sh offers the move on Today, in Settings and in a window when it starts. Signed in, everything syncs first and you sign in again in the Flatpak; otherwise save a backup and choose Import backup on the Flatpak's welcome screen. Then it installs the Flatpak, removes the old version (its data stays as one more backup) and opens the new one.

Updates through Flatpak: the update window shows Flatpak's progress, then Verified by Flatpak (the repository is signed), and Restart starts the new version. The first time, your desktop asks whether LecCheck may update itself. If you chose Deny, or a new version needs new permissions, the window says what to run instead.

A clearer update window: how big the download is before you start; a Check the file step you can watch, which reads the download back and checks it against the signed release, then checks itself off; What's new in its own box with a scrollbar, headings and bold, in English left to right in Hebrew too; and when something fails, what went wrong (no connection, not enough space, a file that doesn't match, Android's installer) instead of "Couldn't update".
Check now opens the update window when there's a new version.
Import backup on the welcome screen, for a new device or the Flatpak.

A sign-in kept by the keyring while the data folder was gone (a new install, or the Flatpak finding the old version's sign-in) looked signed in while nothing synced: an empty device now gets the account's data back, and one with data of its own stays signed out until you sign in.
The update window that opens at startup no longer closes again by itself when LecCheck moves on from its splash screen.
Linux no longer needs WebKitGTK or libsoup.
Settings → Developer → Copy diagnostics says how LecCheck was installed on Linux.

Add on Week like in a calendar: tap an empty spot for an hour there, drag out the time with the mouse, or on a phone long-press and drag (15-minute steps). Quick add opens beside it: pick a course or name a new one right there, weekly or one-time, the type and the room, then Save (with Undo). More options opens the course editor with everything filled in.

Move sessions by dragging (desktop): drag a session to another time or day, or its bottom edge to change when it ends. A weekly meeting asks This week only or Every week, then Undo is offered for a few seconds. Every week moves the sessions' marks along to the new day.

Desktop sidebar like Google Calendar: a raised + Create button replaces Add, and a month calendar shows under the tabs: click a day to open its week; the week you're looking at is highlighted, class days have a dot, and no-class days are dimmed with their name on hover.
The Week grid scrolls by itself when a drag nears its top or bottom.

Linux: no more surprise sign-outs. On a keyring without a password (common with automatic login), GNOME Keyring emptied LecCheck's saved sign-in whenever it re-read its file, because the value contained backslashes, so you came back signed out. The sign-in is now saved in a form without any, and an older one is converted the first time it's read. If you were signed out, sign in once more.

A sign-in that can't be read isn't a sign-out: when the system keyring doesn't answer, LecCheck asks it again, and if it still can't, Account and Today say so with Retry and Sign in again instead of showing you as signed out. Nothing is removed.

Canceling a session drops its reminder. A canceled class could still announce itself: reminders were updated two seconds after a change, and leaving the app (home, Recents, swiping it away) in those seconds kept the old one. They're now updated at once when you leave.
Reminders on screen go away when they're out of date: "class starts soon" for a session you canceled or skipped since, and "how was class?" for one you marked in the app (also last night's).
Skipped ahead, no reminder: a session marked Skipped before it starts gets no "class starts soon".

Sync now shows what it did: the icon turns while it syncs, then the cloud with its check pops in ("Up to date"), or it says it couldn't sync (your changes are kept). It also checks that the connection still works: before, pressing it while synced did nothing at all. With reduced motion the icons just change, and screen readers hear the result.
Click the cloud icon to sync: in the title bar (or the sidebar on wide windows), clicking it syncs now, like Ctrl+R / F5; right-click or long-press opens Settings.
Linux remembers the window size and whether it was maximized: it was never saved.
Settings → Developer's log notes each start's sign-in and why a sign-in was ever removed, and Copy diagnostics includes the sign-in state.
Settings → Developer → Sync now says whether the server answered.
Builds pointed at a local test server keep their own sign-in, so testing can't sign out the installed app.
Moving a meeting to another day kept the session's mark and notes but dropped Counts toward attendance when the new day already had a record, so a session left out quietly counted again.
A failed update no longer draws its steps as if everything had finished.
Contact cards in the course editor line up in Hebrew.

Linux: updates no longer erase your data. LecCheck kept its database and settings in the folder install.sh installs it to, so every update deleted them and you came back signed out with an empty schedule. Data now lives in ~/.local/share/com.leccheck.app, and the next update moves it there first.
Android: opening LecCheck from the home-screen widget no longer shows an error ("no routes for location").

Update window: when a new version is out, a window opens at launch with what's new, and Update shows each step there: the download with its size and speed, the check that the file is exactly the released one, then the install and Restart. Later asks again next time; Skip this version waits for the next one. Updates are now signed: LecCheck only installs releases from a list signed by the release build.

Contacts: a course has its lecturer and teaching assistants, each with a name, role and email, edited in a Contacts row of the course editor. The course page lists them with buttons to send an email or copy the address. A course's lecturer becomes its first contact.

Sessions that don't count: turn off Counts toward attendance on a session (in its details, or right-click) when the course doesn't take attendance in it, like a first lecture. It keeps its status but is left out of the percentage, the streak and the requirement, so 80% of 10 lectures becomes 80% of 9.
Canceled sessions keep their course color with diagonal stripes, instead of turning gray, and have their own color in status icons.

Desktop: a denser layout with smaller corners, one-line title bars and a regular Add button; Settings keeps the sidebar, so the tabs are one click away. On Linux the window reopens at the size you left it, maximized if it was.

A roomier course editor. Meetings are one line each ("Lecture · Sunday, 10:00–12:00 · 201") and open in a sheet (a dialog on wide screens) where the type and how it repeats are menus, and the length shows under the end time. A new meeting can be on several days at once. Short name, code and lecturer wait behind + chips, the color is a dot in the name field, and the attendance requirement, notes and links fold into rows. Wide windows get two columns.

Add from Week: tap an empty spot to add a new course, a meeting of a course, or a one-time session there, with the day and time filled in. The grid always shows at least 8:00–18:00 so there's room to tap.

Course page: sessions are listed by type ("Lecture #3") instead of repeating the course name, and on phones Add one-time session moved to the app bar instead of covering the list. Meetings that start mid-semester or every other week from week 2 now say so.

Today: the class in progress is marked from the Now card only, not listed again under Needs marking. Session rows no longer break mid-detail: the type and day (and the time when it fits) come first, then the room after a pin. The swipe hint goes away once you've swiped, and classes that haven't started yet don't show the "to mark" circle.
Stats: the weekly chart shows each week's percentage and labels its lines (0%, 50%, 100%); the attendance card says it briefly, with the full rule behind an ⓘ button.
Welcome: the language switch moved to the top corner.
